title: Chemistry — Atoms, elements and compounds
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for KS3 Science (chemistry) (status of the source: authored-reviewed-reverified-2026-10-08). Terms and clues: C2#c08 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C2#c16 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; C2#c11 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; C2.4#xt2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C2#q10, C2#q16, C2#q11, C2#q17, C2#q12, C2#q19, C2#q13, C2#x03 (written for the game), C2#q14, C2#q15.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Chemical symbol
items.clue: A one- or two-letter code for an element.

items.label: Change of state
items.clue: Melting, freezing, boiling, evaporating or condensing.

items.label: Conservation of mass
items.clue: The total amount of matter stays the same in any change.

items.label: Balance
items.clue: Laboratory instrument that measures how many grams a sample has

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Yes. Gold's symbol, Au, comes from its Latin name, aurum: a capital first letter, then a lower-case second letter.

questions.stem: Some ice in a sealed bag melts, and a little of the water evaporates. What happens to the mass of the bag and its contents?

options.text: It goes down, as liquids weigh less than solids
It stays the same, as no particles are lost
It goes up, as ice floats, so water is heavier
It goes down, as water vapour weighs nothing

questions.explanation: Yes. Melting and evaporating are changes of state: the same water particles are there, just arranged differently. Nothing gets into or out of the sealed bag, so the mass stays the same.

questions.stem: In the formula H₂O, what does the small 2 show?

options.text: There are two of every atom

questions.explanation: Yes. The small 2 counts the atom just before it, hydrogen. So H₂O has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.stem: In an open beaker, 2.0 g of calcium carbonate (chalk) reacts with 50.0 g of acid. Carbon dioxide escapes, and 51.1 g is left. What mass of carbon dioxide escaped?
questions.explanation: Yes. The mass at the start was 50.0 + 2.0 = 52.0 g. It fell to 51.1 g, so 52.0 − 51.1 = 0.9 g of carbon dioxide escaped.

questions.stem: Methane has the formula CH₄. How many atoms are in one molecule of methane?
questions.explanation: Yes. C with no number means one carbon atom, and H₄ means four hydrogen atoms: 1 + 4 = 5.

questions.stem: Magnesium is heated in a crucible open to the air until it has all turned into white magnesium oxide. None of the powder escapes. What happens to the mass of the crucible and contents?

options.text: It goes up, as its atoms turn into heavier atoms
It goes down, as some magnesium burns away
It goes up, as oxygen from the air joins on
It stays the same, as oxygen gas has no mass

questions.explanation: Yes. Magnesium joins with oxygen from the air to make magnesium oxide. The crucible is open, so the mass of that oxygen is added to the reading.

questions.stem: What does the formula N₂ show?

options.text: Two nitrogen atoms that are not joined up
Two nitrogen atoms joined to each other
A single atom of the element nitrogen

questions.explanation: Yes. N₂ is one molecule made of two nitrogen atoms joined together. Nitrogen gas is an element made of these molecules.

questions.stem: In a sealed tube, 5.6 g of iron reacts completely with 3.2 g of sulfur to make iron sulfide. What mass of iron sulfide is made?
questions.explanation: Mass is conserved: 5.6 g + 3.2 g = 8.8 g, because every atom is still there in the product.

questions.stem: The symbol Co stands for cobalt. What does CO stand for?

options.text: Carbon and oxygen atoms joined together
Carbon and oxygen mixed but not joined
One new atom of carbon and oxygen

questions.explanation: Yes. CO has two capital letters, so it is two symbols: C (carbon) and O (oxygen). It is carbon monoxide, a compound.

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide is CO. Carbon dioxide is CO₂. Which statement is correct?

options.text: They are one compound in different amounts
CO₂ is two CO molecules joined together
Both molecules have the same number of atoms
CO₂ has one more oxygen atom per molecule

questions.explanation: Yes. CO has 1 carbon and 1 oxygen atom; CO₂ has 1 carbon and 2 oxygen atoms. They are different compounds with different, fixed ratios of atoms.
